fia_question: Does the outer iron bridge retaining the V-pocket magnets survive centrifugal load at 19,500 rpm as a SCREENING stress check?

geometry_provenance.controlling_dimensions: state.fpkConcentricGeometry with orchestratorContract quantity fallbacks; magnet size mirrors em_fia_front_kit_case
geometry_provenance.statement: Kit-sized outer iron-bridge ligament from twin rotor OD/ID/active length + EM V-pocket magnet sizing; not the ring screen and not the calculix_smoke_selftest cantilever.

margins.note: SCREENING only against assumed isotropic steel yield (355 MPa). Analytical magnet-on-bridge + coarse CalculiX ligament. Not laminate stack, not fillet burst mesh, not sleeve retention, not fatigue. Never claim release FoS.

material_assumptions.label: Assumed isotropic steel bridge + NdFeB magnet density for centrifugal force — not supplier laminate / magnet / sleeve cards.

model_assumptions: Outer iron bridge thickness = 1.0 mm (matches em_fia_front_kit_case rotor_bridge_mm).
Magnet length/thickness from the same usable-ring clamps as em_fia_front_kit_case.derive_fia_geometry (tilt 20°).
Analytical: one magnet bar mass × ω² × r_cg / (t_bridge × L_active) — idealised membrane ligament.
CalculiX: coarse C3D8 strip at rotor OD, axial length = 25% of twin active length; *DLOAD CENTRIF + magnet-face pressure.
Circumferential ends held in UX+UY (bulk iron); mid-width may bow; UZ fixed on z=0.
No V-pocket fillets, side bridges, sleeve, interference, or laminate anisotropy.
No case / mount / joint / torque-reaction load cases.

release_fos.statement: Screening FoS vs assumed steel yield is informational. Release factor of safety requires signed material cards, pocket fillet detail, and correlated FEA — not closed here.

release_statement: Concept evidence only. No FIA homologation, team interface closure, race evidence or permission to ship. Never claim PASS or closed release FoS from this screening case.

solver.analytical_companion: magnet centrifugal force / (t_bridge × L_active) membrane screen
solver.name: CalculiX CrunchiX
